title: Navattic vs Demoboost vs Storylane Demo Suite (2026)
summary: Navattic vs Demoboost compared: features, pricing, use cases, and G2 ratings, plus a framework for choosing the right interactive demo platform.
body_markdown:
Here is my opinionated take up front: the navattic vs demoboost decision is a false binary. Navattic is the polished, category-leading tool for website and self-guided demos, and Demoboost is the broader full-funnel suite built for presales and larger go-to-market teams. Most buyers I talk to are not actually choosing between those two poles, they are trying to escape slow, static demos and get something interactive live without a three-month project.


I run marketing at Storylane, so I have skin in this game and I will disclose exactly where our product fits and where it does not. But this guide is written to help you decide, not to sell you. I will state prices plainly, cite where each tool wins, and give you a role-based framework so you can shortlist in an afternoon.


> **Definition:** An interactive demo platform captures your real product as clickable, guided screens, then lets you embed, share, and track those demos so buyers can experience the product before a sales call.


The pain that pushes teams into this evaluation is almost always the same. As one buyer put it:


> "The ones we have right now are extremely basic. They are very clearly just, like, presentation slides that have been put together."
>
>
> - a Marketing Specialist at a health tech company


## Navattic vs Demoboost at a glance


Both tools solve the interactive demo problem, but they aim at different buyers. Navattic optimizes for polished, marketing-owned website demos you can ship fast. Demoboost optimizes for full-funnel demo automation with governance, which appeals to bigger presales and revenue teams.


The quick verdict: choose Navattic if a product marketer needs beautiful self-guided demos on the site, and choose Demoboost if presales needs multi-format, live and leave-behind demos across the whole funnel. The table below is more complete than either vendor page, because neither states pricing clearly.


Dimension Navattic Demoboost


Primary use case Website and self-guided demos Full-funnel demo automation


Demo formats Interactive HTML capture HTML, screenshot, video, mobile, live overlay, sandbox


Best-fit team Product marketing, demand gen Presales, sales engineering, partners


Starting price Free Starter; Base ~$500/mo Not published, quote only


Free tier or trial Yes, free Starter (1 seat, 1 demo) No public free tier


G2 rating 4.8/5 (900+ reviews) 4.8/5 (~120 reviews)


Read the G2 numbers with the review count in mind (G2, 2026). Both tools sit around 4.8, but Navattic earns its score across 900+ reviews versus roughly 120 for Demoboost, which is a stronger signal of consistency at scale.


The reviewer mix is worth a glance too. Navattic's reviews skew mid-market at roughly 52% of reviewers (G2, 2026), which fits its polished, marketing-led positioning. Treat that as a hint about where the product feels most at home, not a hard rule.


Use this table as a shortlist filter, not a final answer. If a row already rules a tool out for your primary motion, you can stop reading the rest and go deep on the one that fits.


## What is Navattic?


Navattic is widely seen as the category leader for interactive HTML demos, and it earned that position by making website demos genuinely easy to build and embed. It captures your product pixel-perfect, wraps it in guided tooltips, and publishes it as a self-guided experience for anonymous site visitors.


Its Launchpad demo hub lets you group multiple demos into a single destination, and its analytics track step-level engagement. Navattic connects into the go-to-market stack with 25+ integrations, and in 2026 it shipped a run of AI features aimed at speeding up demo creation.


Buyers respect Navattic but name a real limitation. One summed it up bluntly:


> "Navattic is consistently a top player, but we feel they are pigeonholed on one main format, which is basically a screen-record clone."
>
>
> - a VP of Sales at a SaaS company


Core Navattic strengths:


- Pixel-perfect interactive HTML capture
- Launchpad demo hub for grouping demos
- 25+ integrations including Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Slack
- Step-level engagement analytics
- 2026 additions: Agent Demos, the Copilot suite, and Navattic MCP


## What is Demoboost?


Demoboost takes a wider swing. Rather than focusing on the marketing website, it positions as full-funnel demo automation spanning marketing, sales, presales, customer success, and partner enablement. That breadth is the whole pitch.


It supports more demo formats than most rivals, covering HTML, screenshot, video, mobile, live overlay, and sandbox experiences. It pairs live demo workflows with leave-behind assets, so an SE can run a guided session and then hand the prospect an interactive recap.


For larger organizations, Demoboost leans into governance: templates, permissions, and controls that keep a big team consistent. That governance layer is genuinely useful once you have dozens of demo creators, and it is where Demoboost separates from the lighter, marketing-first tools.


The tradeoff is complexity. All that funnel coverage means more configuration, more roles, and more to maintain, which is a fair price if you truly run demos across every stage. If you only need website demos, most of that surface area sits unused while you still pay to learn it.


Core Demoboost strengths:


- Multi-format demos: HTML, screenshot, video, mobile, live overlay, sandbox
- Full-funnel coverage across marketing, sales, presales, CS, and partners
- Live demo plus leave-behind workflows for presales
- Account-level analytics wired to CRM and revenue workflows
- Enterprise governance for larger teams


## Feature-by-feature comparison


Feature lists blur together, so I grounded the scoring in G2 category data rather than vendor claims (G2, 2026). The pattern is consistent: Navattic wins the polished self-guided experience, and Demoboost wins breadth, live demos, and analytics depth.


Capability Navattic Demoboost


Demo formats Interactive HTML Six formats incl. video, mobile, sandbox


Self-guided demos Excellent Strong


Live and guided demos Limited Excellent


Ease of use Strong, some learning curve Moderate


Learning curve Recurring theme in reviews Steeper, more surface area


Analytics depth Step-level engagement Account-level buyer intent


Integrations 25+ Broad, CRM-centric


Personalization Strong Strong


Demo library and management Launchpad hub Governed library


Security Enterprise-grade Enterprise-grade


AI features 2026 Copilot suite Present


Mobile demos Limited Supported


The honest read is that neither tool is strictly better. Navattic leads on the polished Interactive Product Tour experience, while Demoboost tends to lead on Analytics, Live Demonstration, Guided Demos, and most Demo Automation rows in G2's category data (G2, 2026). Match the winner to your primary motion, not to a total row count.


Two rows deserve extra weight because they drive daily usage: demo formats and learning curve. Navattic's single, focused HTML format is a strength if website demos are the whole job, and a limitation the moment you need mobile, video, or a live overlay in the same tool. Demoboost's six formats buy flexibility, but every format is one more thing your team has to learn and govern.


My advice is to score only the four or five rows that map to your actual workflow. A tool that wins ten rows you will never touch is not the winner, it is a distraction with a longer onboarding.


## Pricing compared: Navattic vs Demoboost


Pricing is where this comparison earns its keep, because neither vendor page lays both tools out side by side. Navattic offers a free Starter tier with one seat and one demo, then paid tiers that have run about $500/mo for Base and about $1,000/mo for Growth, usually on annual commitments. Navattic recently hid its paid-tier prices, which makes upfront budgeting harder.


Demoboost does not publish pricing on its own site, so every plan starts with a sales conversation. Third-party write-ups have floated figures, but reported contract values vary widely and skew higher, which makes upfront budgeting hard without a quote.


Plan Navattic Demoboost


Free tier Starter: 1 seat, 1 demo None


Entry paid Base ~$500/mo Custom quote


Higher tier Growth ~$1,000/mo Custom quote


Contract Annual commitments Custom


Public pricing Recently hidden Not published


Partial or quote-gated pricing is not a minor inconvenience, it changes how fast you can evaluate. A buyer described the downstream pain of opaque quoting on a rival tool:


> "Getting a clear quote from Walnut is like the wild west, every conversation results in a different price point for the same seat count."
>
>
> - a Head of Growth at a fintech company


If budget predictability matters to you, weight this heavily. The tool that states a number lets you shortlist without a sales cycle.


## Ease of use, setup, and support


Ease of use decides adoption more than any feature checkbox, and it is the most common place demo projects stall. Support quality is strong for both tools, so the real differentiator is the learning curve, which comes up repeatedly for Navattic in reviews.


Look at the G2 sub-scores to make this concrete rather than hand-wavy: Ease of Use, Ease of Setup, and Quality of Support (G2, 2026). Navattic scores well but reviewers still flag time-to-competence, while Demoboost has more surface area to learn precisely because it does more.


The buyer reality is bandwidth, not capability. As one implementation lead told us:


> "I didn't have the bandwidth and time to sit down and truly learn the whole app as a whole."
>
>
> - a Training and Implementation Lead at a health tech company


That single sentence should shape your trial. Do not judge these tools by their best-case demo, judge them by how far a busy, non-technical marketer gets in the first hour.


Run the trial with the person who will actually own demos, not with your most technical teammate. Give them a real product screen and a stopwatch, and see who ships a publishable demo first. The tool that respects limited bandwidth is the one your team will still be using in six months.


## Best fit by team and use case


The cleanest way to choose is to map the tool to the team that will own it. Navattic rewards a marketing-led motion where the goal is self-guided demos on the website. Demoboost rewards a presales-led motion with live demos, partner enablement, multi-format needs, and governance.


If you are... Lean toward Choose it if...


Product marketing / demand gen Navattic You want polished website demos live fast


Presales / sales engineering Demoboost You run live demos and need leave-behinds


Partner / channel teams Demoboost You enable external teams at scale


Small team, tight budget Navattic free tier You need one demo without a sales call


Enterprise with governance needs Demoboost You must control many demo creators


Be honest with yourself about who actually maintains demos. If it is one marketer, breadth you never use is a cost, not a benefit. If it is a ten-person SE org, governance you skipped becomes a mess within a quarter.


The other variable is buying stage. A small team that needs one demo live this week is poorly served by a custom-quote sales cycle, so a free tier or transparent pricing wins outright. An enterprise standardizing across regions and business units should weight governance and multi-format support far more than time-to-first-demo.


Notice that these criteria rarely point the same direction. When ease of use and governance pull against each other, decide which one your team will feel every single week, and let that break the tie.


## How they compare on analytics and buyer intent


Analytics is where the two philosophies diverge most sharply. Navattic reports screen-level engagement, telling you which steps of a demo hold attention and where viewers drop. Demoboost pushes toward account-level buyer intent wired into CRM and revenue workflows, which is aimed at pipeline attribution.


The distinction matters because different teams ask different questions. Marketing wants to optimize the demo itself, so step-level data wins. Revenue leaders want to know which accounts are engaged and whether a demo is being shared internally, so account-level intent wins.


Buyers describe exactly this need in their own words:


> "We want to make sure that we can determine when someone's clicked on something, which one is getting the most clicks? Whether or not something is being shared internally."
>
>
> - a Product and Marketing Lead at a cybersecurity company


Pick the analytics model that matches the decision you need to make. If demo optimization is the job, step-level detail is more actionable than an account rollup you cannot act on.


## Where a third option fits: fast, simple interactive demos


Full disclosure: this is us. I would not be doing my job if I let you frame this as a two-horse race, because a large slice of buyers land here for a reason neither incumbent fully answers.


Storylane Demo Suite is built for teams that find Navattic expensive or newly opaque on price and Demoboost too heavy and quote-gated. For a direct feature comparison, see[how Storylane compares to Navattic](https://www.storylane.io/blog/storylane-vs-navattic) . The mechanism is deliberately simple: capture your product with a browser extension, edit the copy screen by screen without engineering, then embed the demo on your website for self-guided discovery with click-level analytics. Our[Demo Hubs](https://www.storylane.io/product/demo-hubs) group those demos into a single destination, and[Sandbox Demos](https://www.storylane.io/product/sandbox-demos) let buyers explore a live-feeling environment.


The speed is the point, and buyers feel it immediately:


> "It was really easy when I, because I recorded it from the extension, it was really easy to like change the text by each like screen section."
>
>
> - a marketing specialist at a health analytics company


**Choose Storylane Demo Suite if:**


- You want self-guided interactive demos on your website that are live within a day, not weeks.
- Transparent pricing matters: you want to evaluate with a free trial before talking to sales.
- You need Demo Hubs to group multiple demos into one destination for passive lead generation.
- Sandbox Demos let your buyers explore a live-feeling environment without engineering overhead.
- Your team is a marketer, not a presales engineer, and you need something you can own and update yourself.


Here is where Demo Suite does not fit, stated plainly. If you need deep enterprise governance across dozens of demo creators, or you want a single vendor to own every presales, CS, and partner workflow end to end, the broader suites deserve a serious look. Demo Suite is the right call when your priority is getting interactive, trackable demos live fast, run by the marketer who owns the site rather than an engineering team.


## Migration and switching considerations


No top-ranking comparison talks about the real cost of switching, and that silence hides the hardest part of the decision. Moving demo tools is not just signing a new contract, it is rebuilding an asset library your funnel already depends on.


Buyers are candid about the internal friction:


> "Getting the business case to actually switch is going to be a bit of a pain in the ass."
>
>
> - a Product Support team member at a cybersecurity company


Before you commit, walk this checklist so nothing surprises you:


1. Rebuild the demo library: inventory every live demo and estimate rebuild effort per demo.
2. Re-embed: find every page, email, and campaign where a demo is embedded and swap it.
3. Re-wire analytics: reconnect tracking, CRM sync, and any attribution reporting.
4. Retrain the team: budget real time for whoever creates and maintains demos.
5. Run parallel: keep the old tool live until the new demos are published and verified.


The takeaway is to weight time-to-first-demo heavily in your trial. For more on evaluating interactive demo platforms, our guide to[building interactive product demos](https://www.storylane.io/blog/interactive-product-demos) covers the key criteria. A tool that gets one real, embedded demo live in a day changes the switching math more than any feature list, because it shrinks the project that scares your team.


## FAQs


**Is Navattic or Demoboost better for presales?**


Demoboost is the stronger presales fit. It supports live and guided demos plus leave-behind assets, and it wins the Live Demonstration and Guided Demos sub-scores on G2 (G2, 2026). Navattic is better suited to marketing-owned, self-guided website demos.


**Does Demoboost publish pricing?**


Not on its own site. Demoboost runs every plan through a sales conversation, and third-party reports of its pricing vary widely, so you will not see a firm number without a quote. If transparent, upfront pricing matters to you, factor that in.


**Can Demoboost replace Navattic for website demos?**


It can, but it is not the same tool for that job. Demoboost can produce self-guided website demos, yet Navattic is more focused and polished for the marketing-led, embed-on-your-site motion. If website demos are your only need, Navattic or a lighter tool is usually simpler.


**Is Navattic free?**


Yes, Navattic offers a free Starter tier with one seat and one demo. Paid tiers have started around $500/mo for Base and $1,000/mo for Growth on annual commitments, though those paid-tier prices are recently hidden.


**Which is easier to learn, Navattic or Demoboost?**


Navattic is generally the faster to learn because it does less and focuses on self-guided demos, though its learning curve is still a recurring theme in reviews. Demoboost has more surface area to master because it spans the full funnel.
